subject: Throughput sizing follow-up FinEx performance targets
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput sizing follow-up - recap & next steps

Hi Sam - great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery so we have aligned inputs for sizing: 

1) Traffic profile
- Steady-state QPS: ~25 req/s
- Peak QPS: ~120 req/s for short spikes (typically 5-15 minutes during earnings/market events)
- Average token output per request: 100 tokens (typical answer)
- Long completions (>=500 tokens): ~5% of requests

2) Latency / streaming SLOs
- First-token p95 target: <300 ms (important for UX)
- Sustained streaming rate: >= 20 tokens/sec for subsequent tokens
- End-to-end p95 for typical reply (~100 tokens): target <6s

3) Concurrency & behavior
- Steady concurrent requests: ~40
- Peak concurrent: ~200 (during spikes)
- ~60% of requests are short Q&A (10-50 tokens) and can be cached/prefix-shared

4) Model & features
- Priority: streaming support + deterministic ordering for real-time feed consumption
- Model target: a medium-to-large open model (we discussed a balanced latency/quality variant)

Next steps from Redwood: we will run a throughput sizing calc (assumptions attached) and propose a config for Dedicated or Hosted with autoscale thresholds + recommended cache/batching settings. Please confirm the numbers above and call out if any of these are off (avg tokens, % long completions, or peak duration).

Attachments: finex_slo_summary.pdf (SLO & assumptions), finex_throughput_calc.xlsx (initial calc)

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Davis <emily.davis@finex.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up - recap & next steps

Hi Rafael - thanks for the clear recap, that looks right overall. A few clarifications: 

- Peak behavior: those 5-15 minute spikes are right. During earnings there can be a few ~30-min windows where QPS stays elevated; allocate for 120 QPS sustained for up to 30 minutes in worst case.
- Streaming: we need a low first-token latency because traders open the app and must see the first line almost instantly. p95 <300ms is our goal but if you can get p90 <200ms that's ideal.
- Long completions: they are closer to 8% for our research workflows (reports + summaries).
- Model: we plan to start on the medium tier and then test quality vs latency; for now assume avg token generation speed target ~30-40 tokens/sec per replica.

Also copying Emily (procurement) to start a thread about potential reserved capacity options if sizing points to Dedicated.

Thanks - Sam
Sam Jenkins
Product Lead, FinEx
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 07:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up - recap & next steps

Appreciate the clarifications, Sam - updated notes and assumptions below; I've updated the attached spreadsheet to show two sizing scenarios (Hosted autoscale vs Dedicated reserved capacity):

Updated assumptions applied in calc:
- Steady QPS: 25 req/s
- Peak QPS: 120 req/s for up to 30 minutes
- Avg response length: 100 tokens (8% long completions assumed at 500 tokens)
- Per-replica generation throughput assumption: 35 tokens/sec (conservative mid-point)
- Batch/caching savings: assume 20% token-cost reduction from prefix caching and batching in steady-state

Initial recommendation (summary):
- Hosted autoscale: suitable if you want fast time-to-value and can tolerate slightly higher unit cost during spikes. Configure burst nodes to handle 120 QPS and set autoscale policy to add capacity above 30 concurrent streams.
- Dedicated baseline: 3-4 medium GPU nodes for steady-state with autoscale pool to add 2-3 extra nodes for 120 QPS peaks (recommend 4-week trial to validate). This assumes 35 tokens/sec per replica and the 20% caching savings - see worksheet 'NodeSizing' in the attachment.

Questions for you: 
1) Can you confirm % of requests that require streaming long-poll updates vs. single-response chat? (we assumed ~15% streaming sessions)
2) Any region constraints (we assumed US-west) or data residency needs?

Attaching: finex_throughput_calc.xlsx (NodeSizing worksheet) and finex_slo_summary.pdf

Next step: propose a 30-minute sizing review on Thu or Fri this week - Rafael/Marissa/Marcus will walk through the calc and recommended config.

Best,
Rafael
